message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season (typically spring and summer). A male will approach a female’s scent-marked territory, often following her scent trail. When he finds her, he may engage in a brief display of dominance—such as roaring or body posturing—to establish his presence. If the female is receptive, she will allow him to mount her. The actual copulation lasts only a few minutes, but the male may stay nearby afterward to guard the female from other males. After mating, the female will usually remain with her cubs, while the male may leave or stay to protect the pride’s territory.
